summary: Grays Harbor County, WA DNR lookout site: 12-ft tower built 1937, 30-ft cab tower in 1942, gone by 1963; footings reported and roadside access.

facts.design: 12' wooden tower (1937), replaced in 1942 by a 30' wooden tower with an 8'x8' cab
facts.status_note: The 1942 tower was removed or destroyed in 1963 (sources differ); Willhite reports the 1942 footings are still there

access.note: Roadside site on the paved Wynoochee Valley Road; Willhite describes roadside parking near the high point; no closure described in the sources read

visit.trail_note: No trail. About 17 miles from Montesano on Wynoochee Valley Road, then park on the roadside near the high point. Willhite has missed the footings several times, and trees were thinned in late 2021.

events.note: 12-foot wooden tower; a 1937 survey party placed it directly above the Mobray Benchmark
30-foot wooden tower with 8x8 foot cab replaced the 1937 tower
Register says the 1942 tower was removed in 1963
firelookout.com and Willhite say the 1942 tower was destroyed in 1963
Registered January 19, 2012, nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says it was removed in 1963; firelookout.com and Willhite say it was destroyed in 1963. The story reports both. No DNR or newspaper record was found to settle it.

sources.title: Mobray Lookout Site - Grays Harbor County

notes_for_editor: Only volunteer registries and one personal site were read; no DNR or newspaper record found. The Weebly index page (washingtonlookouts.weebly.com/mobray.html) lists a separate Aircraft Warning Service station, George 9-9 (1944), which is not this lookout and was left out. Willhite says the Mobray AWS site may be about a mile north; not used. Willhite photo captions (Mobray 1955; 1942 footings photo by Jeff Ruckle) have no image URLs in the cache, so no photos were added. The brief's status 'gone' is correct.
